title: What Factors Explain the Sustainability Orientation of Entrepreneurship? A Comparative International Study
content: The objective of this article is to analyze the factors related to entrepreneurs’ orientation toward sustainability, paying special attention to the environmental, social, and institutional conditions of countries and the characteristics of their entrepreneurial ecosystems. To this end, a comparative study of 30 countries is conducted using indicators from international sources, notably the Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM). The sustainability orientation of entrepreneurship is examined through five indicators that capture different dimensions of entrepreneurs’ social and environmental attitudes, decisions, and priorities. The methodology combines descriptive statistics, scatter plots, and multiple linear regression models. The results reveal significant heterogeneity among countries, both in terms of entrepreneurial activity and across the various dimensions of sustainability orientation, indicating that higher levels of entrepreneurial activity do not necessarily imply a greater incorporation of sustainability criteria. Perceived entrepreneurial capabilities and post-compulsory education show positive and significant relationships with some of these five indicators. In contrast, the general indicators of environmental performance, sustainable development, climate change, and institutional quality do not show statistically significant associations. Taken together, the findings suggest that the sustainable orientation of entrepreneurship is linked to multiple national conditions, among which entrepreneurial capabilities deserve special attention.
